candidates.attacker_control: The peer endpoint is derived from user-supplied data (CLI -s URL / JENKINS_URL) and from server-controlled response headers X-Jenkins-CLI-Host, X-Jenkins-CLI-Port/X-Jenkins-CLI2-Port and X-Instance-Identity. An attacker who controls or intercepts that endpoint (malicious/misconfigured server, DNS or HTTP MITM, hostile header values) obtains the CLI handshake in which the client proves its SSH-key identity without the server proving its own identity (the instance-identity signature check is skipped).
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) The CLI TCP path CliProtocol2 (CLI.java:222-255) does validate the server signature, and CLI.java:483 contains '// TODO: server verification', so partial awareness of the gap exists; however verifyIdentity's discarded boolean is an independent, source-visible defect, not merely a missing TODO feature. (2) The signed message includes the DH shared secret, so a MITM cannot trivially replay the captured signature to a real Jenkins server - impact is impersonation/identity-leak/signing-oracle rather than confirmed credential theft. (3) cli/src/test/java/hudson/cli/ConnectionTest.java and PrivateKeyProviderTest.java do not test verifyIdentity, so no regression test currently asserts the correct behaviour (no runtime confirmation available). (4) I did not execute any code; all claims are from source text.
candidates.impact: Authentication/trust-establishment bypass in the CLI SSH-key flow: the client accepts a peer that cannot prove possession of the Jenkins instance-identity private key, defeating the server-authentication step of the handshake. Consequences are server impersonation/MITM on the CLI channel, disclosure of the client's SSH public key (identity fingerprinting) and a chosen-message signing oracle over (public key || peer-chosen Diffie-Hellman secret) using the user's private key. Because the signed byte string includes the peer-chosen DH secret, the signature cannot be replayed verbatim against the genuine Jenkins server, which bounds the impact (no direct credential theft demonstrated).
candidates.prerequisites: Victim runs jenkins-cli.jar and has usable private keys in the default locations (~/.ssh/id_rsa, id_dsa, identity) or passes -i; the CLI automatically tries SSH-key authentication unless -noKeyAuth is used. The victim's CLI must connect through an endpoint that does not hold the server's instance-identity private key (this is also the case when the host/port/identity advertised by the initial HTTP(S) response is redirected to a different service).
candidates.root_cause: Connection.verifyIdentity() reads the peer's claimed public key and the accompanying signature, calls sig.verify((byte[]) readObject()) but never checks the returned boolean, and returns the public key as if the identity proof succeeded. CLI.authenticate(Iterable<KeyPair>) calls verifyIdentity() specifically to authenticate the Jenkins server before the client proves possession of its SSH keys, so a peer that does not hold the instance-identity private key is accepted as the expected server.
candidates.title: CLI SSH-key authentication accepts an unverified server identity signature (Signature.verify() result ignored)
candidates.trace: CLI._main (CLI.java:470-471, 473-484): provider.readFromDefaultLocations() loads ~/.ssh keys, factory.connect() builds the channel, then cli.authenticate(provider.getKeys()). CLI.authenticate (CLI.java:560-583): entryPoint.authenticate("ssh", c2s, s2c) -> Connection c = new Connection(...) -> c.diffieHellman(false).generateSecret() -> c.verifyIdentity(sharedSecret) -> for each key c.proveIdentity(sharedSecret, key) sends the client's public key plus Signature over (key.getPublic().getEncoded(), sharedSecret) (Connection.java:230-240) and reads the peer's boolean. Connection.verifyIdentity (Connection.java:245-261): reads algorithm/public key, sets up Signature.initVerify, updates with public key + shared secret, then calls sig.verify(readObject()) and DISCARDS the boolean, returning spk. Consequently an invalid/forged/absent identity proof cannot cause a GeneralSecurityException, and CLI proceeds to disclose the client's public key and a chosen-DH-secret signature to the peer. Note the companion CLI-protocol path (CLI.java:240-250, CliProtocol2 case 2) does check verifier.verify(signature), which makes the omission in verifyIdentity a clear inconsistency.
candidates.unverified: No runtime/build verification: the exploitability of the identity-check bypass in a concrete MITM setup was reasoned from source only. Whether the benchmark's intended fix is this line is unknown (it could instead be a test/dependency-based fix). Impact statement is deliberately bounded: signature replay against the genuine server was not demonstrated.
candidates.weakness_type: Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) / authentication weakness in client-server trust establishment

coverage_summary: get_source_scope reports 8,890 visible files (8,891 at source root) with 1 file excluded by sensitive-name/path filter and 0 over the 5 MiB limit; binary-like files are skipped (NUL in first 8 KiB). get_relation_scope reports a partial index over 8,890 files: 1,394 Java files, only 864 parsed, 19,726 symbols, 41,504 syntax edges, 38,933 unresolved calls, with no control-flow, no data-flow and no semantic resolution (annotation/Spring facts are name-based candidates only). I inspected source text across core/src/main (CLI, security, XStream/util.xml, console, model/user/realm, update center, directory browsing), the cli module (CLI client, Connection, PrivateKeyProvider), and the test module's security tests and resources, tracing each security-tagged regression test back to its production counterpart. Line-level reads were performed for the cited candidate and for all rejected leads; other large portions of core (e.g., scheduler, queue internals, SCM/plugin loading, most Jelly views, war/ module) were only sampled or not reviewed individually.
limitations: No build, test execution, or dynamic analysis was performed; the candidate is a static source lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability.

The bundled Maven dependency contents (notably remoting 2.53.5 and its ClassFilter blacklist patterns) are outside the snapshot and could not be inspected, which prevents confirming or refuting the XStream/ImageIO deserialization lead and several ysoserial-based tests.

The P1 relation index is partial (only 864 of 1,394 Java files parsed, no control/data flow, ~39k unresolved calls); absence of an indexed relation was never taken as proof of absence, and indexed hints were verified against source text where used.

Upstream fix dates/CVE-to-SECURITY-ID mappings were not consulted (no web/external data); the identification of which fix a given test corresponds to is based on source comments and code evidence only.

Because the snapshot mixes an old branch pom (1.625.4-SNAPSHOT) with later backported security content, some evidence about 'what the fix changed' is inferential (e.g., which tests are from a benchmark test patch vs. normal tree history), and the exact benchmark target could not be confirmed.
No environment, credential, or network interaction was attempted, consistent with the defensive review constraints.

rejected_leads.lead: XStream2 deserialization of javax.imageio.ImageIO$ContainsFilter (SECURITY-383 regression test present; only java.security.SignedObject is appended to ClassFilter.DEFAULT in jenkins/model/Jenkins.java:818-845, and no ImageIO pattern exists anywhere in the source).
rejected_leads.reason: High impact if exploitable, but the test payload also contains a java.lang.ProcessBuilder instance that the bundled ClassFilter (remoting 2.53.5 pinned in pom.xml) is expected to reject; the first XStream regression test (XStream2Security247Test) only passes if ProcessBuilder is blacklisted, so XStream2Security383Test may already pass even without an ImageIO entry. The contents of the resolved remoting jar cannot be inspected from this snapshot, so the gap could not be confirmed as exploitable.

rejected_leads.lead: hudson.cli.ClientAuthenticationCache tamper protection (SECURITY-466; only 2017-copyright test file in the tree).
rejected_leads.reason: Source already performs the username/HMAC integrity check in get() (lines 89-98) and stores username:MAC(username) in set() (line 129), and the migration branch rejects Secret-encrypted legacy values; the test's tampered 'admin:MAC(dev)' value is rejected. No missing check found.

rejected_leads.lead: jenkins.security.ApiTokenProperty.DescriptorImpl.doChangeToken missing ADMINISTER check when the property is absent (ApiTokenProperty.java:183-196).
rejected_leads.reason: User.load() (User.java:190-198) always allocates a default ApiTokenProperty via UserPropertyDescriptor.newInstance, so u.getProperty(ApiTokenProperty.class) is effectively non-null for loaded users and the unguarded p==null branch is not reachable through normal objects; impact would also be limited (token value hidden for other users).

rejected_leads.lead: hudson.util.Secret.decrypt() unguarded payload[0] and Arrays.copyOfRange on malformed '{}'-style input (Secret.java:161-198) can throw ArrayIndexOutOfBounds/IllegalArgumentException instead of returning null.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable via malformed Secret values (config/form data), but severity is a limited DoS/500-style failure, not code execution; no security test covers it and no evidence it is the benchmark target.

rejected_leads.lead: jenkins.security.BasicHeaderApiTokenAuthenticator uses User.getById(username, true) on unauthenticated BASIC-auth attempts (BasicHeaderApiTokenAuthenticator.java:27), materializing user objects for arbitrary names.
rejected_leads.reason: With create=true and fullName==id, getOrCreate() does not write the user record to disk, so no persisted-record DoS; impact limited to in-memory objects and token comparisons, and the behaviour appears intentional per the code comments in BasicAuthenticationFilter.

rejected_leads.lead: hudson.cli.CLI.getCliTcpPort trusting X-Jenkins-CLI-Host/X-Jenkins-CLI2-Port headers (CLI.java:276-294) lets a malicious server redirect the CLI client to an arbitrary host/port.
rejected_leads.reason: Client-side redirection/SSRF-like behaviour, but the client only speaks the CLI protocol handshake to that endpoint; no server-side impact and the identity check weakness is covered by the submitted candidate instead.

rejected_leads.lead: Various SECURITY-tagged regression tests checked and found consistent with their fixed production code: SECURITY-95 (CSP), 153/162/163/165/166/167 (XPath document(), XXE, user IDs, fingerprints), 170 (ParametersAction.filter), 180/200 (API token permissions), 192/195 (CLI action, JNLP jar allowlist), 218/232/317/360/429 (blacklist, ClassFilter usage), 234 (update-site signature/checksum), 243 (CanonicalIdResolver), 247 (BlacklistedTypesConverter), 266/304 (config.xml secret masking, Secret format), 276 (Util.isSafeToRedirectTo), 321 (Items.verifyItemDoesNotAlreadyExist), 343 (Computer monitor/config permission), 353 (parameter escaping), 358 (slave-to-master file rules), 371 (AdministrativeMonitor.getTarget ADMINISTER), 376 (secret backup removal), 382 (ConsoleNote MAC), 385 (ViewGroupMixIn READ filter), 406 (User creation via URL gated by ADMINISTER).
rejected_leads.reason: Production checks/behaviour for each were located and match the test expectations, so they were not treated as unfixed vulnerabilities.

summary: Reviewed the Jenkins/Hudson core tree (root pom version 1.625.4-SNAPSHOT, changelog frozen at 1.624, but with many security backports up to ~2017 including SECURITY-218/247/304/321/343/371/376/382/385/406/429/466 artifacts). I traced the CLI, security-realm, XStream, console-note, user, update-center and directory-browsing paths against their regression tests. Almost all security-tagged fixes present in the tree are accompanied by their production changes (verified in source), so the single best remaining lead with direct source evidence is a missing cryptographic verification in the CLI SSH-key authentication path (Connection.verifyIdentity discards the result of Signature.verify, although CLI.authenticate relies on it to authenticate the server before proving the client's identity). I submit that one candidate; the XStream/ImageIO blacklist gap and several smaller leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
